_doc: Readable notes of the Ashen highcamp (ADR-0048; items note_<id> in items/ashen.json): what the valley's scavengers and the Remand Program's salvagers saw of the living Ashen - watching the roads from the high timber, taking what comes up them - and the camp's own marks for the taken it keeps.

defs.title: Note on a Drop Flyer
defs.author: R.
defs.body:
(Pencil on the back of a Program supply-drop flyer, folded small and pushed under a stone by the trail.)

To whoever comes up here next -

They've been watching you since the creek. You won't see them. You'll see ash on a rock where somebody sat, and a fire up here every night that never goes out.

We came up after the drop canister that came down in the timber. Wes went first. They let him walk right up to the gate. Then the drum.

They don't want the sick and they don't want the Program. They want what you carry, and they want you gone from their hill.

Go back down. If you won't, don't use the gate. The east wall of the long hut is only a hide over a hole.

- R.

defs.title: Observation Log, Torn
defs.author: Salvager #3318
defs.body:
REMAND SALVAGE PROGRAM - OBSERVATION LOG
Salvager no. 3318. Post: the blind on the ridge above the high timber.

Day 4. Eleven adults, four children. Fires in the long hut and at the gate all night. Someone is always awake.

Day 6. Two of them came down to the river road at first light and sat on the cutbank till noon. Not hunting. Watching the road. Counting the convoy trucks, I think.

Day 9. A trader's cart came up the river road. They let it get to the bend. By dark the cart was in their yard and the trader wasn't anywhere.

Day 11. They keep three of their own in the little hut by the east wall. Chain on the door. The ones inside don't talk anymore. At night the woman with the stripes on her chin sits outside it and sings.

Day 12. They've found the blind. I can smell their fire from here.

(The rest of the page is torn away.)

defs.title: Birch-Bark Slate
defs.body:
(Charcoal on a slab of birch bark, hung on a peg by the chained door, in the Ashen's hand-marks.)

Three hands inside a ring, each with a line drawn through it.
Beside each hand a row of strokes: days. The rows are long, and the newest strokes are fresh.
Under them the pyre, unlit, and a sun coming up behind it.
At the bottom someone has pressed a whole palm in ash and drawn nothing else.

defs.title: Painted Hide
defs.body:
(Ochre and ash on a scraped deer hide, pegged out by the fire, in the Ashen's hand-marks.)

A mountain. On its top a tall frame like a tree with no branches, and beside it a man with a light on his head.
From the frame one straight line runs down through the mountain into a hollow, and the hollow is full of white roots, drawn over and over until the hide is stiff with them.
The roots climb the line. At the top they come out of the man's mouth.
Around the edge many small figures walk with their arms out, all toward the mountain. Between each figure and the next, seven dots.
